interpretation: Refutes the leading hypothesis: with the entire backbone provably frozen/unchanged, LIBERO-Spatial got WORSE (73.33%->16.67%) not better. interpretation: Result contradicts the simple disjoint-offset-fixes-it hypothesis: with the same trainable-backbone treatment as exp0001, disjoint projection offsets should have produced retention >= exp0001's 73.33% if projection-column overlap were the sole interference mechanism. Instead it landed at 50.00%, worse than exp0001, better than exp0002. Per-task pattern is scattered/task-swapping rather than a uniform decline (3 tasks fine in exp0001 dropped to 0%, 3 different tasks weak in exp0001 hit 100%), consistent with either meaningful run-to-run variance on a small 3-trial/task panel or a new instability source from RoboTwin's all-fresh-init projection weights (vs exp0001's partial warm-start via reused/corrupted LIBERO weights). Combined with exp0002 (backbone freezing alone also failed), points toward the shared transformer backbone as an under-isolated interference channel -- no candidate so far has combined disjoint projections with a frozen backbone to test this cleanly. Recommends investigate-fastwam-problem before the next candidate.

interpretation: Completes the 2x2 matrix: overlap+trainable=73.33% (exp0001), overlap+frozen=16.67% (exp0002), disjoint+trainable=50.00% (exp0003), disjoint+frozen=63.33% (exp0004). Freezing the backbone has OPPOSITE effects depending on projection design: hurts with overlapping projections (73.33%->16.67%, no plasticity to compensate for projection corruption) but helps with disjoint projections (50.00%->63.33%, once projection corruption is eliminated, backbone drift becomes the dominant remaining interference channel and freezing removes it too). Confirms disjoint offsets are a real, substantial fix (huge 17%->63% jump isolated in the frozen-backbone regime) and that backbone-level drift is a second, independent interference channel. Still below exp0001's 73.33% and the 90% floor -- exp0001 (imperfect on both projection overlap AND full backbone plasticity) remains the best multi-embodiment retention result, suggesting backbone plasticity may provide some net-positive adaptation benefit that a full freeze forfeits, not yet isolated. task4 (bowl in top drawer) is 0% across every multi-embodiment candidate -- a persistently hard task independent of these design choices. RoboTwin progress check: click_alarmclock 33.3%/33.3% (clean/random) -- the first non-zero RoboTwin result anywhere in this project (exp0001 measured 0.0% everywhere including this exact task); adjust_bottle remained 0.0%/0.0%. Shows the frozen-backbone disjoint-offset recipe can produce real RoboTwin capability, not just avoid forgetting. Recommends exp0005 combine disjoint-offset projections with partial backbone plasticity (e.g. differential LR: much lower for backbone than projections) rather than a full freeze or full train.

interpretation: DECISIVE FINDING: LIBERO-only continued training (zero RoboTwin exposure) degrades LIBERO-Spatial to 23.33% -- the second-worst result of any candidate in the project, worse than 6 of 8 multi-embodiment candidates. This falsifies the multi-embodiment-interference framing as the primary cause of the retention problem that drove candidate selection since exp0002 (projection overlap, backbone drift, mixing ratio). The real driver is a property of continuing to fine-tune this expanded/padded K=21/22 checkpoint, independent of RoboTwin presence. Leading hypothesis: cold-start Adam optimizer instability (weights-only resume means Adam moment estimates restart at zero, and bias-correction amplifies effective step size for the first ~10-50 steps against an already-converged solution) and/or the LR (3e-5) simply being too high for continued fine-tuning of an already-converged checkpoint. Recommends exp0010: same LIBERO-only setup at a 10x lower LR (3e-6) to directly test this.

Found root cause via code inspection: research/tools/expand_checkpoint_for_multiembodiment.py randomly initialized new action_encoder INPUT columns; action_encoder input (noisy_action from flow matching) is genuinely non-zero at padded columns during both training and inference (unlike proprio, which is deterministically zero there), so random weights times real noise injected an untrained perturbation into the shared hidden representation on every forward pass. Fixed by zero-initializing those columns (matching the already-correct head output-row treatment).

But further training past step 1000 shows a real, multi-task-confirmed DECLINE in RoboTwin capability (2 of 4 tasks collapsed to 0% by step 1800) despite LIBERO staying solid (96.7-100%) and training loss continuing to fall -- a classic 'loss improves, closed-loop success does not' signature. Not an LR-schedule-restart artifact alone: turn_switch's collapse (60%->0%) happened entirely within cont1's single uninterrupted schedule. Leading hypotheses: LIBERO/RoboTwin gradient interference at the shared backbone, or open-loop/closed-loop distribution shift (action head overfitting the offline imitation distribution in a way that hurts closed-loop rollout stability). Selected cumulative step 1000 as best-so-far checkpoint; paused training pending diagnosis before designing the next candidate.

interpretation: Decisive result: freezing the shared backbone reversed exp0013's RoboTwin decline entirely. 4-task Clean mean rose from 30.0% (exp0013's declined step-1800 state) to 75.0% after 1000 more frozen-backbone steps, every task at or above its best prior value, LIBERO-Spatial unchanged (96.67%). Strongly supports shared-backbone LIBERO/RoboTwin gradient interference as the primary driver of exp0013's decline (hypothesis 1), though a mid-run click_alarmclock dip (80%->40% at local step 400, recovered by step 1000) leaves some room for a contributing action-head-specific effect (hypothesis 2). New project-best checkpoint, backed up durably. Training extended (cont2, 1000 more steps) given the clearly positive, still-improving trend. UPDATE (full 50-task Clean-only confirmation, n=10): mean success is 12.6%, far below the curated 4-task panel's 75.0% and the 90% target -- only 6/50 tasks clear 50%. The curated panel happened to sample 4 of the model's genuinely strongest tasks, not a representative slice. Combined with the LIBERO-Long regression (87.0% vs exp0012's 95.0% baseline), the honest read is that the gap to the project goal is a training-scale/coverage problem, not a close promotion tradeoff -- next steps should focus on continued/scaled training rather than a promotion decision on this checkpoint. FINAL UPDATE: a second full-50-task rescan (n=5) at cumulative step 4600 -- 2000 steps after the first full scan -- shows 11.6% mean, essentially unchanged from 12.6% at step 2600, despite the curated-panel tasks (click_alarmclock, turn_switch) continuing to improve steadily over the same interval. Nearly the identical ~10-11 of 50 tasks show any capability at both points.
